root_cause.text: In `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c`’s `rxgk_verify_response()`, the RESPONSE authenticator length check was inverted (`auth_len < len` instead of rejecting `auth_len > len`), allowing oversized authenticators to pass into `rxgk_decrypt_skb()` and later trigger `skb_to_sgvec()` with an invalid length.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (auth_len < len)` to `if (auth_len > len) goto short_packet;`, and the CVE description says the function “is supposed to verify that it fits in the remaining bytes” but “the existing check is inverted,” leading to oversized RESPONSE authenticators being accepted and reaching `BUG_ON(len)` in `__skb_to_sgvec()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the auth length validation to reject packets whose declared authentication data is longer than the received buffer.
intent_record.what: In `rxgk_verify_response()`, the comparison against `auth_len` was changed from `if (auth_len < len)` to `if (auth_len > len)` before the existing `short_packet` error path.
intent_record.how: This reverses the length check so the code now rejects responses whose declared authentication length exceeds the available packet length, preventing out-of-bounds parsing of an overlong auth field.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the auth length validation to reject packets whose declared authentication data is longer than the received buffer.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes the inverted authentication length check in rxgk_verify_response(), which is the root cause of the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This is the inverted length check described in the root cause. It incorrectly rejects only when the declared authenticator length is smaller than the received buffer, allowing oversized authenticators to proceed into decryption and later length-sensitive skb processing.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the inverted RESPONSE authenticator length check. It wrongly rejects only when the authenticator length is smaller than the received buffer, instead of rejecting oversized authenticators, which allows invalid lengths to reach rxgk_decrypt_skb() and later skb_to_sgvec().

bic_trace_step.reason: Yes, the shown function body is sufficient because it contains the exact RESPONSE parsing and length check in `rxgk_verify_response()`. The vulnerable construct is present: after reading `auth_len = ntohl(xauth_len);`, it does `if (auth_len < len) goto short_packet;`. This is the inverted check described in the root cause; it should reject oversized authenticators (`auth_len > len`), but this code instead rejects only when the authenticator is smaller than the remaining packet length. There is no compensating bound check before the later call to `rxgk_decrypt_skb(krb5, gk->resp_enc, skb, &auth_offset, &auth_len, &ec);`, so the fix is not present in this version.
